1) Answer

Yes. There is substantial, bipartisan, legislated evidence that Marco Rubio values human rights. Examples:

- He authored and led the Uyghur Forced Labor Prevention Act (S.65, 117th), which blocks imports made with forced labor from Xinjiang; it passed Congress with near-unanimous support and was sent to the President after a bicameral deal he struck with Sen. Jeff Merkley and House partners. ([congress.gov](https://www.congress.gov/bill/117-congress/senate-bill/65?utm_source=openai))
- He sponsored the Uyghur Human Rights Policy Act of 2020 (S.3744, 116th), the first U.S. law focused on Uyghur human rights, authorizing sanctions and reporting on abuses in Xinjiang. ([congress.gov](https://www.congress.gov/bill/116th-congress/senate-bill/3744/titles?utm_source=openai))
- He introduced the Hong Kong Human Rights and Democracy Act of 2019 (S.1838, 116th), which mandates sanctions on officials responsible for rights abuses in Hong Kong and annual U.S. reviews of Hong Kong’s autonomy; it passed with overwhelming bipartisan support. ([congress.gov](https://www.congress.gov/bill/116th-congress/senate-bill/1838/text/is?utm_source=openai))
- He was an original cosponsor of the Global Magnitsky Human Rights Accountability Act (S.284, 114th), creating a global sanctions tool against human rights abusers and corrupt actors. ([congress.gov](https://www.congress.gov/bill/114th-congress/senate-bill/284/cosponsors?utm_source=openai))
- He co-led U.S. efforts on Venezuela: cosponsoring the Venezuela Defense of Human Rights and Civil Society Act of 2014 (PL 113-278) and later sponsoring the 2016 extension (PL 114-194) to keep human-rights sanctions in force. ([congress.gov](https://www.congress.gov/bill/113th-congress/senate-bill/2142?utm_source=openai))
- He served in leadership of Congress’s bipartisan China human-rights watchdog (the Congressional‑Executive Commission on China), using it to document abuses and recommend concrete policy (including bills he later helped pass). ([cecc.gov](https://www.cecc.gov/media-center/press-releases/cecc-commissioners-release-2020-annual-report?utm_source=openai))
- Beyond China and Venezuela, he introduced the North Korean Human Rights Reauthorization Act of 2023 (S.584, 118th) to continue U.S. support for North Korean human-rights programs. ([congress.gov](https://www.congress.gov/bill/118th-congress/senate-bill/584/text?utm_source=openai))
- He co-led the MAHSA Act, signed into law in April 2024, to help hold top Iranian officials accountable for repression after Mahsa Amini’s death. ([padilla.senate.gov](https://www.padilla.senate.gov/newsroom/press-releases/padilla-rubio-bill-to-hold-the-iranian-regime-accountable-signed-into-law/?utm_source=openai))

Taken together—drafting and passing multiple bipartisan human‑rights laws, sustaining sanctions tools, and leading formal congressional oversight on rights—these actions are strong, verifiable evidence that he values human rights in U.S. policy.
